subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Hydraulic Pumps: Creating Flow
description: A 60-second lesson on Hydraulic Pumps: Creating Flow.

hook.text: A hydraulic pump doesn't create pressure. It creates flow. Pressure builds only when the flow meets resistance.

buildup.text: Gear pumps trap oil between teeth and the housing. They're simple, cheap, and handle dirty fluid well.

discovery.text: Vane pumps use sliding blades in a slotted rotor. They deliver smoother flow than gear pumps at moderate pressure.

twist.text: Piston pumps handle the highest pressures — over 400 bar. They're complex, expensive, but unmatched in performance.

climax.text: Variable-displacement piston pumps adjust flow on demand. The system uses only the energy it needs.

punchline.text: The pump moves oil. The load decides the pressure.

quiz.question: What type of hydraulic pump handles the highest operating pressures?
options: Gear pumps with hardened steel teeth and tight clearances
Piston pumps that can exceed 400 bar of pressure
Vane pumps with reinforced sliding blades
